text:
Marta G: Heads up — infra-builder publish job (builder-prod) failed verification in Dedicated: images uploaded but cosign verify fails on nodes, so our GitOps rollouts are stuck. Anyone see this yet? :thinking:

Sam K: I see failing pulls on a few dedicated pools. Logs from kubelet / containerd show cosign verification error when pulling by digest. Quick log: 

```
level=error msg=cosign verify: no signatures found for payload
pulled image: registry.redwood-builds.com/infra/builder:20260318-55
digest: sha256:abc123def456...
```

ci-bot: publish-job/infra-builder-prod #472 failed at 2026-03-18T09:12:07Z — step `sign_and_push` returned non-zero. Logs archived: https://ci.redwood.ci/builds/472/logs

Ivy T: Most likely SBOM/signing step changed output layer order, so manifest list in registry points to different manifest than what cosign signed. We recently landed a change that embeds an SBOM layer as a separate OCI layer (was previously as annotation). Could be that.

Alec W: Another possibility is the registry caching proxy returning an older manifest list while the blobs got updated — I've seen `docker manifest` inconsistencies between region-edge caches and primary. What do the registry push records show?

Sam K: Pushing registry events: primary accepted blobs at 09:11:59, manifest push at 09:12:05. cosign step recorded sig for digest sha256:abc123def456, but nodes see manifest digest sha256:abc123def456 -> cosign says no signature for that digest when verifying local pull. That suggests the manifest list referenced by the tag points to a different manifest in the node's registry mirror.

Marta G: CI job re-push didn't help — retrying with `--no-cache` and forcing manifest push. I'm going to attempt a manual manifest repair: `oras manifest push` followed by `cosign sign --keyring ...` and then `docker manifest push --purge`.

Ivy T: Two-pronged fix we should do: 1) pin base-builder image digests in Dockerfiles to avoid rebuild nondeterminism; 2) make the publish pipeline push a signed manifest list (cosign + `skopeo copy --sign-by`) and include a post-push verify step that does `cosign verify` against the tag (not just the digest). Also add a registry propagation check by pulling from our regional mirror after push.

Sam K: Quick command that helped during debug (local):
```bash
# re-create manifest list and push with signatures
docker manifest create registry/...:TAG \
  registry/...:amd64@sha256:... \
  registry/...:arm64@sha256:...
docker manifest push --purge registry/...:TAG
cosign sign --key ./keys/prod.key registry/...:TAG
cosign verify registry/...:TAG
```

ops-bot: FYI — ArgoCD reported sync failures on `infra-tooling` apps starting 09:15. Several rollouts auto-rolled back per policy.

Alec W: Also found a cached blob issue on us-west mirror. I flushed the CDN cache for the registry path and invalidated the mirror. Re-pushing may be necessary after flush.

ci-bot: re-run trigger: `publish-job/infra-builder-prod #473` started with env `NO_CACHE=1`, `FORCE_MANIFEST_PUSH=1`, `COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1`.

Sam K: After #473 finished, I validated by pulling from a dedicated node in prod: `ctr images pull --plain-http registry/...:20260318-55` and `cosign verify registry/...:20260318-55` — both good. ArgoCD syncs resumed.

Marta G: Root cause summary for postmortem: SBOM layering change + registry mirror cache meant signatures were effectively tied to a different manifest id. Short-term fixes: force manifest push + cache invalidation + post-push cosign verify from regional mirrors. Long-term: pin base digests, move SBOM into an annotation or reproducible layer ordering, and add an integration test in CI that simulates verification from a mirrored pull.

Ivy T: I'll open a PR to pin base images and add the post-push verify step in `ci/publish.sh`. Also adding a small smoke test in the GitOps pipeline that does `cosign verify` after ArgoCD sync.

Marta G: Thanks — please also add a note in infra runbook about `registry cache invalidation` steps and the manual manifest repair commands. We should block auto-rollouts for a short window next time we change SBOM output. :white_check_mark:
